external_audit.opinion_detail: Audit of 2024/25 accounts commenced 4 August 2025 following July 2025 planning activities. Fieldwork underway. Scheduled to complete by end of December 2025 with audit findings to Audit and Risk Assurance Committee 15 January 2026 and final SoA published by 30 January 2026. Backstop deadline for 2024/25 was 27 February 2026. Prior years 2022/23 and 2023/24 received DISCLAIMER OF OPINION by Grant Thornton due to backstop time constraints, NOT due to underlying control failures - explicitly noted in cabinet paper as the auditor unable to gain assurance necessary by backstop date.
external_audit.vfm_conclusion: 2024/25 VfM work in progress. 2021 Grant Thornton VfM Governance Review identified three statutory recommendations - all three LIFTED by Grant Thornton December 2023 follow-up review.
key_risks_in_2024_25_audit_plan: Valuation of land and buildings, council dwellings and investment properties
Valuation of pension fund net liability
Implementation of Oracle Fusion General Ledger (post-implementation review needed)
VfM risk: delivery of housing service - Housing Improvement and Transformation Programme being monitored
VfM risk: Sandwell Childrens Trust £3M deterioration vs forecast outturn (control weakness concern)

commissioners: Kim Bromley-Derry CBE DL (lead, also interim CEO from August 2021)
historical_intervention.trigger: Grant Thornton VfM Governance Review 3 December 2021 identified deeply troubling picture of mismanagement and ineffective scrutiny and accountability arrangements
historical_intervention.sos_finding: Secretary of State agreed Council now meeting Best Value Duty; Commissioners fourth report 7 March 2024 concluded Council ready to move forward without Commissioner support

internal_audit.overall_opinion_detail: In the opinion of Internal Audit, reasonable assurance could be provided that the Council had adequate and effective governance, risk management and internal control processes. Opinion based on work undertaken throughout the year by Internal Audit alongside work by other external bodies. Audits conducted in accordance with Public Sector Internal Audit Standards. Majority of key financial systems work undertaken during SBS-to-Oracle Fusion transition (which temporarily increased audit issues raised and recommendations made).
limited_assurance_subjects: Aids and adaptations - delays in equipping households with required adaptations to support independent living
Use of council procurement cards - follow-up review showed slight improvement; further tightened controls required for transaction documentation
Accounts receivable and capital accounting - discrepancies identified in data transferred between SBS and Oracle Fusion (raised with Oracle Fusion Support team)
Sandwell Community School - governance and financial controls concerns; recommendations made to strengthen arrangements and terms of reference
Fifth subject not enumerated in extracted September 2025 committee minutes - check full Internal Audit Annual Report

strategic_themes.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£38M concentrated)
strategic_themes.rationale: £38M of agency-staff spend across 1 master vendors. Top: HAYS SPECIALIST RECRUITMENT LTD (£38M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of HR + Director of Finance + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£31M baseline)
strategic_themes.rationale: £31M utility spend across 1 suppliers. Top: TOTALENERGIES GAS & POWER LTD (£31M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of Property + Sustainability Lead + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £529M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Annual revenue £661M implies indicative CFR c. £529M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

strategic_themes.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative pay bill £264M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £58M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

strategic_themes.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£66M base)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £66M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

strategic_themes.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£0.7M premium estimate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £0.7M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

strategic_themes.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (186 notices; 1 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
strategic_themes.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 186 notices (42 awarded, £19M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 1 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £130M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: West Midlands Fostering Framework 2020 (ceiling £130M). Matched against ledger: Sandwell Carers Service - AWARD — ceiling £1.5M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.5M; Mortuary Facilities and Pathology Services - AWARD — ceiling £1.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £816.1M; Printing of the Sandwell Herald council newspaper  — ceiling £0.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £1.4M. Aggregate identified actual spend £16888M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Cabinet Member + Section 151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Companies House compliance follow-up (£79M flagged — 1 overdue, 3 dissolved, 1 insolvency-history)
strategic_themes.rationale: Companies House lookup on top-50 suppliers identified £79M of spend with statutory-compliance flags: £24M to suppliers with overdue accounts (1), £42M to dissolved-status companies (3), £13M to companies with insolvency history (1). NOTE: Some matches are CH fuzzy-search false positives (e.g. school, government-body name collisions) and need human verification. After verification, real flags = (a) credit-risk review on overdue accounts, (b) contract-cleanup on dissolved entities (records still on ledger but supplier extinct — risk of duplicate-payment leakage), (c) PCR 2015 Reg.57 discretionary exclusion review on insolvency-history suppliers in active contracts.

strategic_themes.title: Refund / credit-note management + contract dispute resolution (£39M, 2,858 rows)
strategic_themes.rationale: 2,858 negative-amount rows totalling £39M — refunds, credit notes, contract reversals. Volume signals correct ledger capture, but proactive levers exist: (a) contract management review on top recurring refund counterparties, (b) duplicate-payment pre-detection, (c) energy-bill credit-management automation. Typical 5-10% reduction in refund volume + faster reconciliation = 10-30bp net cash improvement.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Internal Audit + Treasury

strategic_themes.title: Audit + recover £50M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £50M across 5,230 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

strategic_themes.title: Investigate £90M in flagged split-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE flagged £90M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.
